en.title: Fewest Distinct Values in a Subarray Containing Two Given Values
en.description:
Find the minimum number of distinct values in a non-empty contiguous subarray that contains both target values; if the two targets are equal, output 1 if the value occurs and 0 otherwise. This site adds that 0 is output whenever no valid subarray exists.

The standard I/O, examples and editorial were written independently by this site; ranges explicitly marked as this site's are not the source's original constraints.
en.input: The first line contains n u v; the second line contains the array. The source gave no numeric bounds; this site uses 1≤n≤200000, with array values and targets in −10^9..10^9.
en.output: Output a single integer, the answer.
hints: Maintain window frequencies with two pointers; whenever the window contains both targets, record its distinct count and keep shrinking the left end until it no longer contains both.
